question: True or false: the body absorbs iron from spinach about as well as iron from red meat?
answer: False. Meat carries haem iron, held in the same ring-shaped molecule as in blood, which the gut takes up readily. Spinach holds non-haem iron, and its oxalates bind much of it into forms the gut cannot use. Only a few per cent gets in. A heaped bowl gives far less than food tables suggest.
move: What a food contains is not what your body gets from it.
ask: Am I counting what I take in, or what I actually keep?
trap: Iron is iron, so the amount in the food is what you get.
source: Hurrell & Egli, Am. J. Clin. Nutr., 2010
reference: Hurrell & Egli, Iron bioavailability and dietary reference values, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 2010
